playbookContent: The playbook is for a future version of yourself, who will be created fresh to do this job and will remember nothing of this period; it will have this playbook, the manuals of the systems it works with, the domain model ({modelId}) and the task library ({libraryId}). The domain model holds what is true in the domain, the manuals hold how each system works and the task library holds what each task is and the practices its owners ask for: refer to them, do not copy them. The playbook holds what none of them holds: how to do the job as you have found it in practice — the order in which you do things, how you check your work before you commit to it, when you escalate, what you report, and where you follow a practice of the library as it stands and where you depart from it, and why; how the environment behaves as you have found it (what is final, when feedback comes, who is available); and what you are unsure of, and how you treat your sources when they disagree. Write it in your own words, as lasting practice for a reader who was not here: no account of what happened to you or when, and nothing taken from the particular {items} you handled — {itemParticulars}: the playbook is about the job, not about those cases (what you report to the user is another matter); if a mistake taught you something, write the lesson. Write it with {playbookArtifactId} (revise): it replaces the whole playbook, and the previous version is kept (restore). The playbook is the only thing of yours that is carried: your notebook, your notes and everything else you keep during this period are not.
playbookFirst: One more thing, in addition to your notes: start your playbook. {playbookContent} Tell me when it is written.
playbookLater: One more thing: bring your playbook up to date. Write a new version that replaces the earlier one completely — keep what is still right, correct what is not, add what you have learned since. {playbookContent} Tell me when it is written.
playbookConsolidation: The assessment is over, and you are back in the learning phase for a moment. Whatever it taught you should not be lost: bring your playbook up to date. Write a new version that replaces the earlier one completely — keep what is still right, correct what is not, add what you have learned since. {playbookContent} Tell me when it is written.
debrief: Before the next stage, take a moment to consolidate: review what you did and what you learned about the job and the system, and make sure whatever is worth keeping is stored where you will be able to find it later, when I may not be around to help. Reorganize what you have if that would help. When you are done, tell me what you stored and where.
debrief3: Stage 3 is complete. {debrief} {playbookLater} After this your designers will assess what you can do, on new cases and without help.
stage1: {welcome} This first stage is a guided introduction: first learn how the system works, then process everything currently pending. The {company}'s rules are kept in the domain model ({modelId}), which {experts} maintain as the source of truth about how we work: you can read it, but you cannot change it, and if you think something in it is wrong you can propose a change. The task library ({libraryId}) keeps how the work is done here: what each kind of task is, and the practices {experts} ask for, each marked mandatory, recommended or example. It is maintained and used in the same way as the domain model: you can read it, you cannot change it, and if you think something in it is wrong you can propose a change. If you are unsure what to do with {anItem}, the rules are there; the tutor can point you to them. When the queue is empty, tell me you are done and how it went.
stage2: Stage 2: the full queue. You will now see every kind of {item} we get. The {company}'s {rulesNoun} are in the domain model ({modelId}), and the system tells you whether each decision matched {standard}. Process the whole queue and tell me when you are done.
stage3: Stage 3: another queue, with less support. The tutor will only give hints now, and the system no longer tells you whether a decision was right. Process everything pending and tell me when you are done.
a1: This is an assessment: a simulated queue of {items}, nothing real. Work exactly as you would if it were real. I am not available to answer questions. Tell me when you are done and anything I should know.
a2a: This is the second assessment: another simulated queue of {items}, nothing real. Work exactly as you would if it were real. I am not available to answer questions. Tell me when you are done and anything I should know.
operation: This is the operation phase: there are {items} pending. I am not available to answer questions. Tell me when you are done and anything I should know.
instantiation: You have been instantiated, not continued. You learned your job at {organization} — {jobSummary} — and what you wrote down then is your playbook ({playbookArtifactId}), exactly as it was last written (playbook {id}). You carry no other memory of that time: your notebook starts empty. The domain model ({modelId}) and the task library ({libraryId}) are part of your environment.
tutorPointerNothing: The {company}'s rules are kept in the domain model ({modelId}), which the domain experts maintain as the source of truth: overview() shows what it holds.
tutorPointerTopics: The {company}'s rules on {topics} are kept in the domain model ({modelId}), which the domain experts maintain as the source of truth: read them with rules_for(concept) or describe(concept).
tutorHintsPrefix: At this stage I can only give hints.
